items.stem: A pump has an MTBF of 950 hours and an MTTR of 50 hours. What is its approximate inherent availability?

options.rationale: This under-states availability; the correct ratio is 950/1000.
This is the unavailability fraction, not availability.
Availability cannot be 1.0 when repair time is non-zero.

items.stem: An asset shows a random (constant) failure rate and has a redundant standby. Which TWO maintenance choices are most defensible? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Condition monitoring to detect the onset of failure
options.rationale: Correct: for random failures, condition-based tasks can catch functional failures without assuming wear-out.

options.text: Run-to-failure given the redundancy and low consequence
options.rationale: Correct: with a standby and low consequence, letting it run to failure can be the lowest-cost valid strategy.
Scheduled replacement does not help a constant failure rate and wastes remaining life.

options.text: Do nothing and remove it from the asset register
options.rationale: Removing it from the register loses visibility; it still needs a managed strategy.

items.explanation: Correct: for random failures, condition-based tasks can catch functional failures without assuming wear-out.

items.stem: A machine's annual maintenance cost has risen each year and now exceeds the annualised cost of a replacement. What does this indicate?

options.text: The asset has likely passed its economic replacement point
options.rationale: Correct: when rising upkeep exceeds the annualised cost of a new asset, replacement is economically justified.

options.text: The asset should always be kept because it still runs
options.rationale: Still running is not the test; total cost over time is.

options.text: Maintenance budgets should simply be increased
options.rationale: Increasing budget ignores the cheaper replacement option.
Rising maintenance cost typically signals declining, not improving, reliability.

items.explanation: Correct: when rising upkeep exceeds the annualised cost of a new asset, replacement is economically justified.
